questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully achieved a soft landing on the Moon on which date?
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander successfully soft-landed on the Moon's south polar region on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to achieve a lunar soft landing and the first to land near the lunar south pole. 14 July 2023 was the launch date, not the landing date. 5 September and 10 August are incorrect dates.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the G20 Summit held in India in 2023:

(i) It was held in New Delhi under India's G20 presidency.
(ii) The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 at this summit.
(iii) The summit adopted the 'New Delhi Leaders' Declaration'.
(iv) It was the first G20 summit ever held in India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All statements are correct. The G20 Summit was held in New Delhi on 9-10 September 2023 (i). The African Union was admitted as a permanent member (ii). The summit adopted the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (iii). It was indeed the first time India hosted a G20 Leaders' Summit (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India launched its first solar observation mission named Aditya-L1 in September 2023.
Reason (R): Aditya-L1 is positioned at the first Lagrangian point (L1) between the Earth and the Sun to continuously observe the Sun without eclipses.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023. Reason (R) is also correct — the L1 point allows uninterrupted observation of the Sun. The Reason explains why the mission is significant and why L1 was chosen — to continuously observe the Sun without any eclipse interruption. Option B is wrong because (R) explains the purpose of (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following international events of 2023-2024 with their host countries:

Column I:
(a) COP28 Climate Summit
(b) ICC Cricket World Cup 2023
(c) FIFA Women's World Cup 2023
(d) BRICS Summit 2023

Column II:
(i) South Africa
(ii) India
(iii) United Arab Emirates
(iv) Australia and New Zealand

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: COP28 was held in Dubai, UAE (a-iii). ICC Cricket World Cup 2023 was hosted by India (b-ii). FIFA Women's World Cup 2023 was co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand (c-iv). BRICS Summit 2023 was held in Johannesburg, South Africa (d-i). Option B swaps UAE with India and misassigns others. Option C incorrectly places Cricket WC in Australia/NZ. Option D misassigns COP28 to South Africa.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following countries were admitted as new members of BRICS in 2024?

(i) Iran
(ii) Saudi Arabia
(iii) Ethiopia
(iv) Argentina

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Iran, Saudi Arabia, and Ethiopia were among the new BRICS members that joined in January 2024 (along with Egypt and UAE). Argentina was initially invited but its new government under President Milei decided not to join BRICS. Options B and D incorrectly include Argentina. Option C excludes Saudi Arabia which did join.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was linked with which country's instant payment system 'PayNow' in 2023?
questions.explanation: India's UPI was linked with Singapore's PayNow in February 2023, enabling real-time cross-border fund transfers between the two countries. Japan has its own payment systems but no UPI-PayNow style link at that time. Australia and the UK also have not been linked with UPI in this manner.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Ayodhya Ram Mandir:

(i) The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was inaugurated on 22 January 2024.
(ii) The ceremony is known as the 'Pran Pratishtha' of Lord Ram's idol.
(iii) The temple was built at the site where the Babri Masjid once stood.
(iv) The Supreme Court's verdict paving the way for the temple was delivered in 2019.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct. The Ram Mandir was inaugurated on 22 January 2024 (i). The ceremony was called 'Pran Pratishtha' (ii). It was built at the disputed site in Ayodhya (iii). The Supreme Court delivered its landmark verdict in November 2019 (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was appointed as the Chief Justice of India in November 2024?
questions.explanation: Justice Sanjiv Khanna was appointed as the 51st Chief Justice of India in November 2024, succeeding Justice D.Y. Chandrachud. Justice D.Y. Chandrachud was the 50th CJI who retired. Justice B.R. Gavai and Justice Surya Kant are other senior judges but were not appointed CJI at that time.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India conducted general elections to the 18th Lok Sabha in April-June 2024.
Reason (R): The Indian general elections are the largest democratic exercise in the world, involving over 960 million eligible voters.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India's 18th Lok Sabha elections were held in seven phases from April to June 2024. Reason (R) is also correct — Indian elections are the world's largest democratic exercise with about 968 million eligible voters. However, (R) does not explain (A) — the elections were conducted because the 17th Lok Sabha's term was ending, not because of the large voter base. Option A is wrong because the reason doesn't explain why elections were conducted. Option C is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor' (IMEC) was announced at which summit in 2023?
questions.explanation: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) was announced at the G20 Summit in New Delhi on 9 September 2023. The BRICS Summit was held in Johannesburg but IMEC was not announced there. The SCO Summit in 2023 was virtual, not in Goa. The UNGA did not see this announcement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's semiconductor manufacturing push:

(i) India approved the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) to build semiconductor fabs.
(ii) The Tata Group announced semiconductor fab projects in Gujarat and Assam.
(iii) The mission aims to make India completely self-reliant in chip manufacturing by 2025.
(iv) The total outlay for semiconductor incentives exceeds ₹76,000 crore.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — India approved the India Semiconductor Mission. Statement (ii) is correct — Tata Group announced semiconductor/OSAT fab projects in Gujarat (Dholera) and Assam (Jagiroad). Statement (iv) is correct — the government allocated over ₹76,000 crore for the semiconductor programme. Statement (iii) is incorrect — complete self-reliance by 2025 is not the target; the timeline extends much further as fabs take years to build.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following awards announced in 2024 with their recipients:

Column I:
(a) Bharat Ratna 2024 (one of the recipients)
(b) Nobel Peace Prize 2024
(c) Ramon Magsaysay Award 2024 (Indian)
(d) Padma Vibhushan 2024 (one recipient)

Column II:
(i) Nihon Hidankyo (Japanese organization)
(ii) L.K. Advani
(iii) Koneru Humpy
(iv) Veerendra Heggade

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: L.K. Advani was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2024 (a-ii). Nihon Hidankyo, a Japanese organization of atomic bomb survivors, received the Nobel Peace Prize 2024 (b-i). Koneru Humpy, Indian chess grandmaster, received recognition/awards (c-iii). Veerendra Heggade, head of Dharmasthala, received the Padma Vibhushan (d-iv). Option B swaps Advani with Veerendra Heggade. Option C misassigns the Nobel Prize. Option D incorrectly places Nihon Hidankyo as Bharat Ratna recipient.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which country hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympic Games were held in Paris, France from 26 July to 11 August 2024. Japan hosted the 2020 Olympics (held in 2021). The United States will host the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. Australia will host the 2032 Olympics in Brisbane.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's Gaganyaan mission:

(i) It is India's first crewed space mission by ISRO.
(ii) It aims to send Indian astronauts (Gaganauts) to low Earth orbit.
(iii) The mission has already been successfully completed.
(iv) Indian astronaut candidates have received training in Russia.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight programme. Statement (ii) is correct — it aims to demonstrate human spaceflight to low Earth orbit. Statement (iv) is correct — Indian astronaut candidates (IAF pilots) have undergone training at Russia's Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre. Statement (iii) is incorrect — the crewed mission has not yet been completed; uncrewed test flights have been planned/conducted.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Digital Personal Data Protection Act' was passed by the Indian Parliament in which year?
questions.explanation: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in August 2023. 2022 saw the withdrawal of the earlier Personal Data Protection Bill. 2024 is after the Act was already passed. 2021 is when earlier iterations were being discussed.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are initiatives launched/expanded by the Indian government in 2023-2024?

(i) PM Vishwakarma scheme for traditional artisans
(ii) Ayushman Bharat expansion to cover all senior citizens above 70
(iii) PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (rooftop solar)
(iv) Mission Amrit Sarovar for pond rejuvenation

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: PM Vishwakarma was launched in September 2023 (i — correct). Ayushman Bharat expansion to senior citizens above 70 was announced in 2024 (ii — correct). PM Surya Ghar scheme for rooftop solar was announced in Budget 2024 (iii — correct). Mission Amrit Sarovar was launched in 2022, not in 2023-2024 (iv — incorrect as it predates the timeframe significantly). Options B and C include Mission Amrit Sarovar which was earlier.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sweden and Finland joined NATO in 2023-2024, ending decades of non-alignment.
Reason (R): Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 prompted both countries to seek NATO membership for collective security.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Finland joined NATO in April 2023 and Sweden in March 2024, ending their long-standing non-aligned status. Reason (R) is correct and explains why — Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine directly prompted both Nordic nations to abandon their historical neutrality and apply for NATO membership. Option B is wrong because (R) is the direct cause of (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, commissioned in September 2022, is named:
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant (IAC-1) is India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier, commissioned on 2 September 2022. INS Vikramaditya is a modified Kiev-class carrier bought from Russia. INS Vishal is a proposed future carrier, not yet built. INS Viraat was a decommissioned carrier (formerly HMS Hermes).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Women's Reservation Act (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam), providing __________ percent reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state assemblies, was passed in 2023.
questions.explanation: The Women's Reservation Act (128th Constitutional Amendment) provides 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. It was passed in September 2023. 50% would be half, which was not the approved figure. 27% is the OBC reservation percentage and not related. 40% is not the correct figure.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following international organizations with developments in 2023-2024:

Column I:
(a) WHO
(b) ISRO
(c) UNSC
(d) IMF

Column II:
(i) Declared end of COVID-19 as a global health emergency (2023)
(ii) Launched Aditya-L1 solar mission
(iii) India demanded permanent seat reform
(iv) Approved 16th General Review of Quotas

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: WHO declared the end of COVID-19 as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2023 (a-i). ISRO launched Aditya-L1 (b-ii). India has pushed for UNSC permanent seat reform (c-iii). IMF approved the 16th General Review of Quotas (d-iv). Option B swaps WHO with ISRO. Option C misassigns ISRO to UNSC reform. Option D incorrectly places IMF quotas with WHO.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'One Nation, One Election' proposal in India aims to:
options: Hold Lok Sabha and all state assembly elections simultaneously
Merge all election commissions into one body
Conduct elections only through electronic voting machines
Reduce the number of political parties to one per state
questions.correctAnswer: Hold Lok Sabha and all state assembly elections simultaneously
questions.explanation: The 'One Nation, One Election' proposal advocates holding simultaneous elections for Lok Sabha and all state assemblies to reduce election expenditure and governance disruptions. 'Merge all election commissions' is wrong — there is already one Election Commission. 'Only through EVMs' is wrong — that's about the mode of voting, not timing. 'Reduce political parties' is wrong — that would violate democratic principles.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Israel-Hamas conflict that began in October 2023:

(i) Hamas launched an attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.
(ii) The International Court of Justice (ICJ) ordered provisional measures regarding the conflict.
(iii) India unequivocally supported one side in the conflict from the beginning.
(iv) The conflict led to a major humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023. Statement (ii) is correct — the ICJ ordered provisional measures in January 2024 in a case filed by South Africa. Statement (iv) is correct — the conflict caused massive civilian casualties and humanitarian crisis in Gaza. Statement (iii) is incorrect — India called for de-escalation and took a balanced approach, condemning terrorism while also expressing concern for civilian casualties.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Indian state conducted its assembly elections in November-December 2023, resulting in the BJP winning with a large majority?
questions.explanation: BJP won a large majority in Madhya Pradesh assembly elections held in November 2023. In Rajasthan, BJP won but it was not an unprecedented large majority in context. In Telangana, Congress won, not BJP. In Chhattisgarh, BJP won but Madhya Pradesh saw the largest winning margin. The question specifies 'large majority' which best fits MP where BJP won over 160 of 230 seats.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL), approved for modernization as part of India's semiconductor mission, is located in:
questions.explanation: The Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL) is located in Mohali, Punjab. It is being modernized under the India Semiconductor Mission to produce chips for strategic needs. Bengaluru has many tech companies but not SCL. Hyderabad has semiconductor design centres but not SCL. Gandhinagar is where the Tata OSAT plant is being set up, not where SCL is located.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India abstained from voting on multiple UN General Assembly resolutions related to the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Reason (R): India has historically maintained a policy of strategic autonomy and non-alignment in geopolitical conflicts.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India abstained from several UNGA votes on the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Reason (R) is correct and explains India's abstention — India's foreign policy tradition of strategic autonomy and independent decision-making guided its neutral stance. Option B is wrong because the policy of strategic autonomy directly explains the abstention. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Uniform Civil Code (UCC):

(i) Uttarakhand became the first state to pass a UCC bill in 2024.
(ii) UCC is mentioned in the Directive Principles of State Policy (Article 44).
(iii) UCC aims to replace personal laws of all communities with one common set of laws.
(iv) Goa already has a form of common civil code since Portuguese rule.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. Uttarakhand passed the UCC bill in February 2024 (i). Article 44 of the Constitution mentions UCC under DPSP (ii). UCC aims to have uniform laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance for all citizens (iii). Goa has a common civil code inherited from the Portuguese Civil Code (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's rank in the FIFA Men's Football World Ranking as of 2024 is approximately:
questions.explanation: India's FIFA ranking has been hovering between approximately 100-125 in recent years (around 2024). Between 50-70 is incorrect — this range includes much stronger footballing nations. Between 130-160 places India too low. Between 70-100 is slightly higher than India's actual ranking.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about India's Vande Bharat Express trains?

(i) They are semi-high speed trains manufactured in India.
(ii) They operate at a maximum speed of 160 km/h.
(iii) The first Vande Bharat Express ran between New Delhi and Varanasi.
(iv) They are manufactured by Chinese companies under license.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Vande Bharat trains are indigenously designed and manufactured semi-high speed trains. Statement (ii) is correct — they have a maximum operational speed of 160 km/h. Statement (iii) is correct — the first Vande Bharat ran on the New Delhi-Varanasi route (launched February 2019). Statement (iv) is incorrect — they are manufactured by the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai, not by Chinese companies.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: India's GDP growth rate for the financial year 2023-24 was approximately __________ percent.
questions.explanation: India's GDP growth rate for FY 2023-24 was approximately 8.2% as per the second advance estimate by NSO. 6.5% was a lower estimate given earlier by some agencies. 7.0% was below the final figure. 5.8% is significantly lower than the actual growth achieved.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) came into effect in which year?
questions.explanation: The India-UAE CEPA came into effect on 1 May 2022 after being signed in February 2022 during a virtual summit. 2023 is incorrect — by then it was already operational for a year. 2021 saw negotiations but not the final agreement. 2024 is too late.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Agnipath scheme:

(i) It is a recruitment scheme for the Indian Armed Forces announced in 2022.
(ii) Recruits under the scheme are called 'Agniveers'.
(iii) The service period under Agnipath is 4 years.
(iv) All Agniveers are permanently absorbed into the forces after 4 years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Agnipath was announced in June 2022. Statement (ii) is correct — recruits are called Agniveers. Statement (iii) is correct — the service tenure is 4 years. Statement (iv) is incorrect — only up to 25% of Agniveers are retained for longer service; the remaining 75% are released after 4 years with a service fund.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India's total installed renewable energy capacity crossed 190 GW by 2024.
Reason (R): India has committed to achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030 under its climate targets.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India's installed renewable energy capacity (including large hydro) has crossed 190 GW. Reason (R) is also correct — India has a 500 GW non-fossil fuel target for 2030. However, (R) does NOT explain (A) — crossing 190 GW is a fact of cumulative installations over years, not caused by the 2030 commitment alone. The target is an aspiration, not the reason the capacity exists today. Option A is wrong because the target didn't cause the achievement. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following recent Indian defence acquisitions/developments with their descriptions:

Column I:
(a) Tejas MK-1A
(b) INS Vikrant
(c) S-400
(d) BrahMos

Column II:
(i) Indigenous aircraft carrier
(ii) Light combat aircraft
(iii) Supersonic cruise missile (India-Russia joint venture)
(iv) Air defence missile system from Russia

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Tejas MK-1A is the improved version of India's indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (a-ii). INS Vikrant is India's indigenous aircraft carrier (b-i). S-400 Triumf is the Russian-made air defence missile system acquired by India (c-iv). BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia (d-iii). Option B swaps Tejas with INS Vikrant. Option C misassigns INS Vikrant. Option D incorrectly categorizes Tejas.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Kavach' system in Indian Railways is designed to:
options: Replace diesel engines with electric ones
Provide free WiFi on all trains
questions.explanation: Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system that prevents collisions by automatically applying brakes if the driver fails to respond to signals. 'Increase speed to 300 km/h' is wrong — that would require separate high-speed rail infrastructure. 'Replace diesel with electric' is about electrification, not Kavach. 'Free WiFi' is a separate connectivity initiative.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Digital India programme:

(i) DigiLocker allows citizens to store government documents digitally.
(ii) UMANG app provides access to government services on mobile.
(iii) CoWIN was the platform used for COVID-19 vaccination registration.
(iv) Digital India was launched in the year 2020.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — DigiLocker stores digital copies of government documents. Statement (ii) is correct — UMANG provides a single platform for government services. Statement (iii) is correct — CoWIN was the platform for COVID vaccination registration and certificates. Statement (iv) is incorrect — Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015, not 2020.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which country became the newest member of the European Union in recent years?
questions.explanation: Croatia is the most recent country to join the EU, becoming its 28th member on 1 July 2013 (and joining the Eurozone in January 2023). Ukraine has applied for EU membership but has not yet joined. Serbia is a candidate country but not a member. North Macedonia is also a candidate, not yet a member.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's merchandise exports (in US$ billion) over recent years:

| Year | Exports |
|------|--------|
| 2020-21 | 292 |
| 2021-22 | 422 |
| 2022-23 | 447 |
| 2023-24 | 437 |

In which year was the percentage growth in exports over the previous year the highest?
questions.explanation: 2021-22 growth: (422-292)/292 × 100 = 44.5% (highest). 2022-23 growth: (447-422)/422 × 100 = 5.9%. 2023-24 saw a decline: (437-447)/447 × 100 = -2.2%. 2020-21 cannot be computed without 2019-20 data. The massive 44.5% jump in 2021-22 was due to recovery from COVID-related disruptions.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correct about India's Jan Dhan Yojana?

(i) It is a financial inclusion programme for banking the unbanked.
(ii) Over 50 crore accounts have been opened under the scheme.
(iii) Account holders receive a RuPay debit card.
(iv) The scheme was launched in 2014.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: All statements are correct. Jan Dhan is a financial inclusion programme (i). Over 50 crore accounts have been opened as of 2024 (ii). Account holders receive a RuPay debit card with accident insurance (iii). It was launched on 28 August 2014 by PM Modi (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 replaced which previous education policy?
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 replaced the National Policy on Education 1986 (modified in 1992). The Right to Education Act 2009 is a legal act, not a policy document that NEP replaced. The Kothari Commission (1964-66) informed the 1968 policy but wasn't directly replaced by NEP 2020. The National Knowledge Commission was an advisory body, not an education policy.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan:

(i) It is a digital platform for integrated infrastructure planning.
(ii) It integrates 16 ministries for multimodal connectivity projects.
(iii) It was launched in October 2021.
(iv) It focuses exclusively on road construction projects.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — PM Gati Shakti is a GIS-based digital platform for integrated planning. Statement (ii) is correct — it integrates 16 ministries for coordinated infrastructure development. Statement (iii) is correct — it was launched on 13 October 2021. Statement (iv) is incorrect — it covers all modes of infrastructure (roads, railways, ports, airports, waterways, telecom) — not exclusively roads.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following countries with their recent political developments (2023-2024):

Column I:
(a) Argentina
(b) Bangladesh
(c) United Kingdom
(d) Pakistan

Column II:
(i) Keir Starmer became Prime Minister
(ii) Sheikh Hasina was ousted from power
(iii) Javier Milei elected as President
(iv) Shehbaz Sharif became Prime Minister

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Javier Milei was elected President of Argentina in November 2023 (a-iii). Sheikh Hasina was ousted from power in Bangladesh in August 2024 (b-ii). Keir Starmer became UK PM in July 2024 after Labour won elections (c-i). Shehbaz Sharif became Pakistan's PM in March 2024 (d-iv). Option B swaps Argentina with Bangladesh. Option C swaps Bangladesh with UK. Option D misassigns Argentina.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's first underwater metro rail tunnel was inaugurated in which city?
questions.explanation: India's first underwater metro tunnel runs under the Hooghly River in Kolkata (East-West Metro corridor). It was a landmark engineering achievement. Mumbai has an underwater tunnel for metro planned but Kolkata's was first. Chennai and Delhi do not have underwater metro tunnels.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's position in different global indices (2024 approximate ranks):

| Index | India's Rank (approx.) |
|-------|----------------------|
| Global Innovation Index | 40 |
| Ease of Doing Business | 63 |
| Human Development Index | 134 |
| Press Freedom Index | 159 |

In which of the above indices does India have the best (lowest number) ranking?
questions.explanation: India's best ranking is in the Global Innovation Index at approximately 40th. Ease of Doing Business at 63rd is second best. Human Development Index at 134th is poor. Press Freedom Index at 159th is India's worst ranking. The lower the rank number, the better the position.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Atal Setu (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link) connects Mumbai to:
questions.explanation: The Atal Setu (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link), India's longest sea bridge at 21.8 km, connects Mumbai (Sewri) to Navi Mumbai (Chirle). It was inaugurated in January 2024. Thane is connected to Mumbai by other routes. Pune is about 150 km away, connected by expressway. Lonavala is a hill station, not connected by a sea bridge.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's space achievements in 2023-2024:

(i) ISRO successfully tested the cryogenic engine for Gaganyaan.
(ii) Chandrayaan-3 discovered sulphur on the lunar surface.
(iii) India launched the XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) in January 2024.
(iv) India became the second country to land on the Moon's south pole region.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — ISRO tested cryogenic engines as part of Gaganyaan preparations. Statement (ii) is correct — Chandrayaan-3's rover Pragyan confirmed the presence of sulphur on the lunar surface. Statement (iii) is correct — XPoSat was launched on 1 January 2024. Statement (iv) is incorrect — India was the FIRST (not second) country to successfully land near the Moon's south pole.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Indian cricketer became the first batter in history to score 50 centuries in international Test cricket?
questions.explanation: Sachin Tendulkar holds the record of 51 Test centuries (and 100 international centuries combined), making him the first and only batter to score 50+ Test centuries. Virat Kohli has around 29-30 Test centuries. Rohit Sharma has fewer Test centuries. Sunil Gavaskar scored 34 Test centuries.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Lakhpati Didi' scheme announced in 2023 aims to:
options: Create 2 crore women earning over ₹1 lakh annually through self-help groups
Provide ₹1 lakh cash grant to every rural woman
Train 1 lakh women as commercial pilots
Give pension of ₹1 lakh per year to elderly women
questions.correctAnswer: Create 2 crore women earning over ₹1 lakh annually through self-help groups
questions.explanation: The Lakhpati Didi scheme aims to empower women in Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to earn over ₹1 lakh per annum through skill development and livelihood support. The target was 2 crore women. 'Cash grant to every rural woman' is incorrect — it's about earning, not direct transfer. 'Train as pilots' is fabricated. 'Pension of ₹1 lakh' is incorrect — it's about income generation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has been adopted by several countries for their digital payment infrastructure.
Reason (R): UPI provides real-time, instant payment between bank accounts through a mobile platform at zero transaction cost.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — UPI has been adopted/linked by countries like Singapore, France, UAE, Sri Lanka, etc. Reason (R) is correct — UPI enables real-time bank-to-bank transfers via mobile at minimal/zero cost. The Reason explains why countries adopted UPI — its efficient, low-cost, real-time nature makes it attractive for adoption. Option B is wrong because UPI's features explain its international adoption. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of Vande Bharat Express trains operational in India:

| Year | Number of Vande Bharat trains |
|------|------------------------------|
| 2019 | 1 |
| 2020 | 2 |
| 2022 | 4 |
| 2024 | 100+ |

By what factor did the number of Vande Bharat trains approximately increase from 2019 to 2024?
questions.explanation: From 1 train in 2019 to 100+ in 2024, the increase is approximately 100 times (100/1 = 100). 50 times would mean only 50 trains. 25 times would mean only 25 trains. 200 times would mean 200 trains which exceeds the actual number.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following is the theme of India's G20 presidency (2023)?

(i) 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'
(ii) 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'
(iii) 'Make in India, Make for the World'
(iv) Both (i) and (ii) reflect the same theme

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: India's G20 presidency theme was 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' which is the English rendering of the Sanskrit concept 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family). Both (i) and (ii) are the same theme in different languages — option (iv) correctly identifies this. 'Make in India, Make for the World' is not the G20 theme. Option (i) alone doesn't acknowledge that (ii) is also the theme. Option (i) and (ii) only doesn't recognize they are the SAME theme.
